public_rationale: Zitron said that just over a year after ChatGPT and DALL-E appeared, these tools were 'not particularly useful for anything.' Controlled studies from that window show clear practical gains. A peer-reviewed randomized experiment in Science (July 2023) found ChatGPT cut time on professional writing tasks by 40% and raised quality by 18%. An NBER field study of 5,179 customer-support agents (revised November 2023) found a generative AI assistant raised issues resolved per hour by 14%, and by 34% for novice workers. These are sizeable, measured benefits on real work tasks. They contradict the plain reading that the tools had no meaningful use. His wider worries about reliability and economic value are separate claims and are not judged here.
limitations: The evidence covers text and chat assistants, not image generators like DALL-E.
The task studies are narrow. They do not show broad economic returns.
The Science abstract was read through a Stanford repository listing because science.org blocked access.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI products such as ChatGPT and DALL-E are interesting but not particularly useful for anything.

statement.excerpt: we keep running into the problem that these things are interesting, surprising, but not particularly useful for anything.

from_speaker: "just over a year into the existence (and proliferation) of ChatGPT, DALL-E, and other image generators"
our_interpretation: Plain reading: in the roughly 15 months after ChatGPT launched, generative AI products such as ChatGPT and DALL-E had no meaningful practical use for real tasks.

Well-designed studies showing clear, measured gains on real work tasks from these tools during that window would contradict the claim. A broad usefulness claim needs only one solid counterexample domain to fail.
'Not particularly useful' is softer than 'useless', so small or doubtful gains would not count against him. Large, statistically clear gains would.
criteria.support_condition: Credible studies or data from late 2022 to February 2024 showing that ChatGPT, DALL-E or similar tools gave no meaningful practical benefit on real tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible controlled studies from late 2022 to February 2024 showing large, measurable productivity or quality gains from generative AI tools on real work tasks.
